newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall on Kremlin row nervousness.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall on Kremlin row nervousness.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell amid uncertainty over a power struggle between Russia's security chief and interior minister, dealers said on Thursday.

On Wednesday Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accused Alexander Lebed of plotting to seize power. President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman said today the Krelin leader had not yet decided how to react to the row.

"What is going on is not good for Russia, especially ahead of Eurobond issue. Everybody believes the country will be all right some day but at the moment the mood is more downward than upward," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
Dealers said the third, fourth and fifth tranches had been hit most on mainly foreign selling. But they added prices were periodically finding support at lower levels, also from the West.
"These are good levels to buy for the country with a (high speculative) rating," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
"But London and New York are generally afraid while local banks prefer not to open positions, although some of them were buying," he added.
Dealers said the direction of the market would depend entirely on further political news in the rest of the week.
